highlights: Today is focus-first: one calm “Start here” instruction appears before remaining work, summaries, quiet-contact prompts and reflection tools.
People is now a clearer directory. Adding a person lives in the header and empty state, while the persistent note bar remains the single prominent capture action.
Your first note can be saved before you add anyone. Person context is optional, so setup can never block or lose a thought.
Shared text, shared photos, the home-screen widget and the quick-settings tile now use the same activity-owned one-shot capture path, preventing dropped or repeated intake events.
Settings visibly stays selected while its sheet is open, and person rows retain readable open counts and quiet-follow-up accessibility cues.

Includes the post-2.2 reliability line: release-build and connected-device CI, migration/startup hardening, safe shared-image OCR, restorable automatic Drive backups, and cleanup of historical raw-note outbox copies.

Send to a group, from the note bar. Type an @mention for a rank, a station or everyone (for example “@si”, “@station:Subedari”, “@all”) and the note offers to send it to that group instead of just saving it. Mentioning one person by name, like “spoke to @ramesh”, stays an ordinary note.
Google Drive backup actually works. “Back up now” and “Restore from backup” previously did nothing at all when tapped — no dialog, no error, no backup. Both now prompt for your passphrase and run.
Sending no longer marks an instruction done. Dispatching a message only means it went out; you decide when the task is actually finished.

Your recovery phrase is protected from accidental replacement. Opening the recovery-phrase screen used to silently generate a new phrase, quietly invalidating whatever you had written down. It now warns you first.
Search handles hyphens correctly — badge numbers and case numbers like “QAP-7734” are found again.
Important dates: the delete control said “Cancel” and deleted immediately with no confirmation. It now says “Delete” and asks first.

Fixes for the audience picker (no way back once you drilled in, duplicate rows for the same rank spelled differently, missing screen-reader labels), the onboarding sample-data toggle (only the switch was tappable, not its label), a duplicated sentence on the onboarding screen, and a debug-only fixture reload that could overwrite a fresh first run.
21 defects found by an adversarial on-device audit, each fixed with a regression test. 661 unit tests.

Brand rename: package com.baton.app → com.kaavalan.note; class identifiers Baton* → Kaavalan*. The launcher label, widget label, and tile label are now KaavalanNote (single CamelCase token). The app icon (KAAVALAN shield on cream) is unchanged.

Hierarchy polish: ContactSyncService + ContactPickerSheet (import device contacts into the People list from the Home empty state), RosterBuilder + AudienceResolver + MentionAndTagParser + DeliveryService for the people → instructions → mentions → roster → dispatch round-trip, E.164 phone normalization via TelephonyManager, DispatchComposerSheet + DispatchViewModel with race-safe rosterReady gating.

EXPECTED_SCHEMA in DatabasePreflight aligned to v16 (the hierarchy work had left it pinned to the v15 baseline; on a fresh install the preflight was flagging a brand-new DB as 'missing body/kind columns').

Priority.URGENT restored to the v2.1.1 priority enum — the hierarchy merge had dropped the constant; existing on-device instructions with priority=URGENT were crashing RoomInstructionRepository.toDomain() at Enum.valueOf.
release-v2.1.1 security stack (P0 PKCE / P1 BackupCrypto / P2 CharArray + schema verify + PII redaction) is in the build — release/v2.1.1-security is an ancestor of this branch.

Bug fixes: device-owner bootstrap now runs synchronously before the preflight (was a GlobalScope race that surfaced a spurious 'DB error' banner on first launch); AutoMirrored ArrowBack/Send icon migration; the Unchecked cast on HomeViewModel's combine result is gone via a type-safe filterIsInstance.
Test suite: 578/578 effective pass (5 VaultCryptoCharArrayTest ignored because argon2kt 1.6.0 has no host JVM fallback; see docs/v2.1.1_test_environment.md to enable them locally).

Google Drive backup: WhatsApp-style. The local DB stays on the device; a backup goes to your Google Drive's hidden app folder; you can restore on a new device. Backups are encrypted with a key derived from your 12-word recovery phrase BEFORE upload — Google cannot read the bytes.
Daily auto-backup: a WorkManager job runs every 24h, encrypts the latest snapshot, and uploads to Drive. The passphrase is set once on first manual backup.
SQLCipher preflight is now a full read + write + read round-trip (catches the 'write silently corrupts' case that the v2.0.2 SELECT-1 missed).
Removed the pre-v8 destructive migration. Users upgrading from v1.7.x or earlier will still see data preservation through the new 6 explicit MIGRATION_2_3..MIGRATION_7_8.

Settings → Google Drive backup section: 'Sign in with Google' / 'Back up now' / 'Restore from backup' / 'Sign out'. The OAuth flow uses AndroidX Browser Custom Tabs (no play-services-auth dep needed).
521 unit tests pass; :app:assembleDebug builds clean.
Settings → Privacy → About: build info, privacy posture, source repo link.
SQLCipher DB-error recovery: a 'Database error — Erase and restart' banner appears if the preflight detects a corrupt DB. The 'Erase all data' flow is the recovery path.
Settings → Privacy → Audit log: lists recent entries and runs the SHA-256 chain verifier on demand.
Settings → Import: round-trip a v1.x CSV/JSON export back into the local DB. Re-importing is idempotent.
RetentionWorker firing test pins the daily retention contract (old rows deleted/redacted, recent survive).
BackupManager restore e2e test pins the export → wipe → restore round-trip.
Bug fix: Hilt 'HttpClient' MissingBinding that would have crashed the in-app 'Check for updates' (latent in v1.9.x).
Threat model rewritten to document the local-only architecture and the ML Kit OCR third-party surface.
Operations runbook: recovery flows for 'data is gone', 'app crashes on launch', 'I forgot my vault PIN', and migration from v1.x.
500 unit tests pass; :app:assembleDebug builds clean.
BREAKING: All Supabase cloud sync is removed. The app is now local-only.
All data lives in a SQLCipher-encrypted Room DB on the device. No remote auth, no account, no email.
The only outbound network call is 'Check for updates' against the public GitHub Releases API (no auth, no PII).
Removed: multi-device sync, MCP cloud server, MindAnchor cross-app state, in-app sign-up/sign-in.
The sync_queue table is kept in the schema for forward-compat but no rows are written in v2.0.
Settings → Privacy → What's new (replaces the auto-shown 'What's new' modal — v1.6.0 design rule).
Threat model rewritten to document the local-only architecture and the ML Kit OCR third-party surface.
490 unit tests pass; :app:assembleDebug builds clean.
Pre-v8 users MUST back up via Settings → Export before updating — the v2-v7 destructive migration will wipe the local DB.
Quick Note widget now has 3 sizes: 2x2 capture button, 4x2 with today's count, 4x4 with recent notes
In-app 'What's new' screen on first launch after a version bump
Recovery-phrase flow is now end-to-end tested (wipe device + 12-word restore + 56 people + 200 instructions)
Single shared Supabase client (was 4, now 1) — fewer battery + bandwidth use at cold start
Tag refresh failures now surface a visible error in the Home screen (was silent)
A11y: every interactive element has a contentDescription; touch targets are 48dp minimum
APK size budget set to 40MB; release build is 38MB (debug is 47MB)
Quick Note widget — one-tap capture from the home screen (no need to open the app)
Tag refresh errors now surface a visible error (was silent)
Single shared Supabase client (was 4, now 1)
Atomic instruction creation (4-table write now in a single transaction — no partial data on crash)
Auto-reseed is debug-gated (release builds no longer wipe user data on first launch)
One-tap 'Report a problem' mailto in Settings — embeds the latest crash log in the body
Production & enterprise gap audit: 18 items identified, 3 closed in v1.9.9, 3 closed in v1.9.10, 5+ more in v1.9.11
a11y improvements: drive label, onboarding polish
